title: Yosemite National Park, California
seoTitle: Charter Bus to Yosemite National Park, California
excerpt: A charter bus to Yosemite National Park removes the park's worst problem: parking. Where coaches can go, which vehicle fits, and how to plan the valley day.

extraImage.alt: Giant sequoias in Mariposa Grove with a group walking the path between them

body.text: Yosemite Valley is seven miles long and about a mile wide, and on a summer Saturday it holds more cars than it has places to put them. That single fact is the strongest argument for a charter bus to Yosemite National Park: the group arrives together, gets dropped at the trailhead, and never joins the queue circling the day-use lot at Curry Village.
The valley, and everything outside it

Most first-time groups spend their day on the valley floor, which is the right call. El Capitan, Half Dome, Yosemite Falls, Bridalveil Fall and the Merced River are all within a few miles of each other, connected by a flat loop road and a free park shuttle. It is the one part of Yosemite where a group with mixed walking ability can all have a good day.

Outside the valley, Mariposa Grove holds around five hundred mature giant sequoias and sits near the South Entrance, about an hour from Yosemite Village. Glacier Point gives the classic view down onto Half Dome and is worth the drive if the road is open. Tunnel View, on the way in from the south, is the photograph — five minutes, one pullout, and the whole valley in front of you.
Roads that close, and reservations that catch people out

Glacier Point Road and Tioga Road are seasonal, typically opening between late May and early July and closing with the first serious snow. A group planning a Glacier Point sunset in early June should have a valley alternative ready. Yosemite has also run timed-entry reservation systems in recent summers; the rules change year to year, so check the park's current requirements when you set the date rather than assuming last year's applied.
Which charter bus suits a Yosemite trip

items: Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/motor-coaches) handles the approach roads and the valley loop, and there is designated bus parking near Yosemite Village. The most comfortable choice for the two to four hour drive in.
Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) has an easier time on the winding approach from the south and at the smaller Mariposa Grove and Glacier Point lots.
Ten to fourteen: a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) suits a small group and parks anywhere a car does, which in Yosemite is worth more than it sounds.

body.text: Whatever the size, the approach is long enough that an on-board restroom changes the day. There is very little between the gateway towns and the park gate, and a group of fifty stopping unplanned costs half an hour.

From San Francisco it is about four hours to the valley; from [Fresno](/locations/california/fresno) around two and a half via the South Entrance; from [Merced](/locations/california/merced) about two. Groups often stage overnight in [Oakhurst](/locations/california/oakhurst) or [Mariposa](/locations/california/mariposa), which turns a punishing day trip into a comfortable one and puts you at the gate before the queue builds.

If you are searching for charter bus rental near me for a Yosemite trip, ask whether the driver has run the park before. The approach roads are steep and winding, the valley has specific bus routing, and a driver who already knows where the coach parking is saves the group forty minutes at the start of the day.
The free shuttle and mixed-ability groups

Yosemite Valley runs a free shuttle on a continuous loop around the valley floor, stopping at the major trailheads, the village and the lodges. It is the reason a group with very different walking abilities can still have a good day together: the strong walkers take the trail to Mirror Lake while everybody else rides two stops and meets them there.

Several of the headline sights are also genuinely accessible. The path to the base of Lower Yosemite Fall is paved and short, Bridalveil Fall has a short paved approach, and the Mariposa Grove has an accessible boardwalk section. Tell us in advance if anyone in your group uses a wheelchair or has limited mobility and we will route the day around the stops that work rather than the ones that photograph best.

items: April to June: the waterfalls are at full volume from snowmelt, which is the single best reason to time a trip. Yosemite Falls can be nearly dry by late August.
September and October: warm days, thin crowds, and the most reliable weather of the year.
July and August: everything is open and everything is full. Start early and plan the valley for the morning.
November to March: quiet and often beautiful, with the valley open year-round, but the high roads are closed and chains may be required.

body.text: Give the valley a full day rather than half of one. A workable shape is Tunnel View on the way in, a drop at Lower Yosemite Fall, two hours free on the valley floor with the shuttle, lunch at Yosemite Village, and Mirror Lake or the Merced meadows in the afternoon. Groups that try to add Mariposa Grove and Glacier Point to the same day spend most of it on the bus.
